name: Centro and the Alcazaba
tagline: Below the Moorish fortress, with the cathedral and the tapas streets
description: Almeria's centre below the Alcazaba, the largest Muslim fortress built in Spain after the Alhambra, running from the cathedral through the tapas streets to the Rambla. It is compact, flat and walkable, with the port and the seafront promenade at the bottom.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the Alcazaba, the cathedral and the tapas circuit on foot
pros: The Alcazaba and the cathedral within minutes
The tapas circuit, where a drink comes with food
Flat, walkable and close to the port
cons: The highest rents in the city
Busy in the evening on the tapas streets

name: Zapillo
tagline: The beach district east of the port
description: The residential district running along the beach east of the centre, with a long promenade, apartment blocks facing the sea and a settled local population. It is where Almeria actually swims, ten minutes from the historic centre on foot, and rents are moderate for a seafront address.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a beach at the door at a sensible rent
pros: Long beach and promenade directly there
Ten minutes on foot to the centre
Moderate rents for a seafront position

name: La Chanca and the Old Quarters
tagline: The painted houses on the hill below the fortress
description: The old fishing and gypsy quarter climbing the hill west of the Alcazaba, with brightly painted houses, some cave dwellings still in use and a strong community identity. It is the most photogenic part of Almeria and the poorest, with a reputation that residents consider outdated and visitors should treat carefully.
bestFor: Stays wanting genuine character and the lowest central rents
pros: Painted houses and cave dwellings, genuinely unusual
cons: Poorest district in the city with a difficult reputation
Housing stock is old and variable
Worth local advice before choosing a street

name: Cabo de Gata (35 km east)
tagline: The volcanic park and the emptiest beaches on the coast
description: The natural park east of the city, a volcanic coast of cliffs, dunes and beaches with almost no development, salt pans holding flamingos and villages like San Jose and Las Negras where a few hundred people live. It is the reason many people come to this province at all.
bestFor: Stays wanting the emptiest beaches in Spain, with a car
pros: Flamingos on the salt pans and volcanic cliffs
Diving and snorkelling in the marine reserve
cons: Thirty-five kilometres out and a car is essential
Very few services in the villages
Busy in August despite the protection

name: Tabernas and the Desert (30 km north)
tagline: Europe's only desert, and the western film sets
description: The badlands north of the city, the only true desert in mainland Europe, where a great many spaghetti westerns were shot in the 1960s and several sets survive as attractions. The landscape is genuinely striking, and the enormous solar research platform sits in the middle of it.
bestFor: Short stays and day trips rather than a base
pros: The only desert landscape in mainland Europe
cons: Thirty kilometres north with almost no accommodation
Nothing to do beyond the landscape and the sets
